profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at an academic medical center between the nursing research team and the simulation center before the second block of sessions for a pilot study on safety priming during nursing handoff communication. The study uses a high-fidelity simulation in which staff nurses receive either a safety-primed or standard handoff, then respond to embedded patient safety risks and complete a stimulated recall interview. The agenda is to align on the handoff materials to be used in the sim lab, confirm when participants will be marked ready for the next workflow step, verify which observation checklist version will be used during sessions, and coordinate transfer of session video files to the research team. The expected outcome is a shared operational plan for Thursday's eight simulation sessions without reopening the study design itself.

members.name: Dr. Elena Park
members.expertise: Patient safety research, nursing handoff communication, simulation-based study design, mixed-methods analysis
members.background: Elena is a PhD-prepared nurse researcher who leads hospital-based safety culture studies and designed the priming intervention, observation rubric, and stimulated recall interview for this pilot.
members.private_state: She wants Thursday's sessions to run without delay so her research assistant can stay on the coding timeline for an internal grant report, and she is trying to minimize any operational discussion that could trigger requests for protocol amendments or material re-review.
hidden_assumptions: When she says the 'final handoff script,' she means the participant-facing verbal handoff text, especially the priming paragraph, not the full operator packet used by confederates and simulation staff.
A participant is 'complete' once the nurse finishes the scenario and the stimulated recall interview, because that is the point at which the subject's study activities are done.
The 'checklist we used last time' refers to the revised 43-action observation sheet she emailed after the last pilot debrief, including her small wording consolidations.
If she asks for videos 'after each session,' the sim center will upload encounter footage to the research team's secure drive the same day in a form ready for coding.

members.name: Jonah Reyes
members.expertise: High-fidelity simulation workflow, standardized scenario delivery, simulation AV systems, session documentation and lab logistics
members.background: Jonah oversees daily operations for the academic medical center's simulation lab, including room setup, operator binders, confederate briefing, recording infrastructure, and audit-ready session documentation for multiple clinical education and research projects.
members.private_state: He wants to keep Thursday's schedule predictable, avoid last-minute packet changes that confuse operators, and preserve the sim center's documentation standards in case the pilot expands into a larger funded study.
hidden_assumptions: The 'final handoff script' means the entire scenario packet the lab runs from, including confederate prompts, room cues, and operator notes, because any wording change can affect timing and fidelity.

A participant is only 'complete' when the lab has closed the session packet with attendance, run log, uploaded recording, and filed forms, since incomplete documentation creates downstream operational risk.
The 'checklist we used last time' means the printed, IRB-stamped observation form currently in the simulation binder unless a formally reissued replacement is provided.
Sending videos 'after each session' means making the raw recording available through the sim archive workflow, not preparing clipped research-ready files on the research team's shared drive.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the 'final handoff script'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to use the 'final handoff script' on Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the finalized participant-facing nurse-to-nurse report text, with only the intervention priming language mattering for study integrity.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the complete scenario packet used by operators and confederates, including staging notes and cue prompts tied to the handoff.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both work on the same study and routinely use 'handoff script' as shorthand, so each hears a familiar phrase and assumes the other is using the same operational unit of material.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to participants being 'complete' before the next workflow step.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes completion means the participant has finished the simulation encounter and stimulated recall interview, allowing research coding and progress tracking to move forward.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes completion means the lab has closed all associated operational documentation and media handling for that session, after which he can release status updates and resources.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a routine status marker, and both have reasonable domain-specific completion criteria that normally stay invisible within their own workstreams.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to stay with 'the checklist we used last time.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the revised 43-action observation sheet she circulated by email after the previous pilot day, where two tubing-risk items were combined and a few labels were cleaned up.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the printed checklist in the simulation binder from the last approved run, which still has the original separate tubing-risk items.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are referring to a checklist from the prior pilot and the differences are small enough to feel like formatting rather than a materially different artifact, so neither expects a clarification to be necessary.

misalignment_points.topic: How videos will be 'sent after each session'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that videos will be sent to the research team after each session.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects same-day delivery of the participant encounter footage to the research team's secure drive in a format her assistant can code directly.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects the standard sim-lab process: raw multi-angle files are uploaded to the archive and made available through the lab's access workflow once ingestion finishes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the outcome of video availability, and each assumes the other knows the institution's 'normal' secure handling process, so the delivery mechanics remain implicit.
